title: Canonical two-fibre square and higher-image comparison on big etale stack sites
statement:
Fix a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme] and the small-skeleton convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal X$, $\mathcal Y$ and $\mathcal Y'$ be categories fibred in groupoids over $\mathit{Sch}/S$, with based functors and two-fibre products as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Use precisely the big etale rings, all module sheaves, precomposition $h^*$, right-adjoint direct image $h_*$ and injective-resolution higher direct images $R^ih_*$ of [def-sfb-stack-big-etale-module-functors]. Precomposition is additive and preserves finite limits and colimits: sections and kernels are computed objectwise and cokernel sections lift locally over etale covers. Degree zero of an injective resolution gives an injective embedding, so these module categories have enough injectives. The adjunction $h^*\dashv h_*$ is the selected adjunction defining that recorded right adjoint.

For $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ and $b:\mathcal Y'\to\mathcal Y$, put $\mathcal X'=\mathcal Y'\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$, with projections $a:\mathcal X'\to\mathcal X$ and $f':\mathcal X'\to\mathcal Y'$. The two-fibre product is again fibred in groupoids. Its second projection is the comma second projection; the vertical comparison isomorphism gives its equality over the base. For original site arrow and object universes $v,w$, the comma product's objects are in $\max(v,w)$; the source-universe extension of the recorded precomposition and direct image applies to the two projections, with unchanged section coefficient bound $\max(u+1,v,w)$. No relation between $v$ and $w$ is imposed.

Define the unique natural transport $a^*f^*\to f'^*b^*$ whose component on a module $M$ at a comma object $(y',x,\alpha:b(y')\simeq f(x))$ is the restriction $M(\alpha):M(f(x))\to M(b(y'))$. It is invertible, with inverse restriction along $\alpha^{-1}$. The canonical underived comparison $b^*f_*\to f'_*a^*$ is the counit mate of the inverse of this transport, using the recorded adjunctions. For every $i\in\mathbf N$, define $b^*R^if_*\to R^if'_*a^*$ by deriving this mate and taking cohomology, using exactness of $a^*$ and $b^*$. Auxiliary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] are the standard localization. This definition asserts no higher-base-change isomorphism.

This is stable pointed-curve extension, not stable modification of a specified target pair. Moduli prerequisite: projective compactification with prime-to-characteristic level structure and its universal stable family, used before taking the closure of a generic lift. Projectivity of the unpointed stable coarse moduli scheme. Supporting input: Projective geometric quotients of closed stable loci for PGL. Affine-chart proof of the projective PGL quotient: Affine PGL quotients with closed orbits and zero-dimensional stabilizers. Supporting affine-quotient step: Finite inertia gives an adequate coarse moduli space. Supporting input to the finite-inertia coarse-space construction: Passage from invariant global power liftings on the affine rank charts to adequate moduli spaces, then etale descent to the glued map. Flat scalar-section comparison needed in the descent of a power lying in the image of a global algebra map; this does not assert adequate-moduli locality. General cohomological input: preservation of locally quasi-coherent modules and flat comparison maps under qcqs stack direct images. Supporting input: Smooth descent criterion for preservation by higher direct images. Per-degree consequence of the derived big-etale base-change input, used to localize the target by smooth affine charts. Canonical big-etale structure-module categories, precomposition and counit-mate comparison required to state this per-degree input.
